svg.title: Routing and dispatch — orchestrate.decide, router.route_request, both fallbacks and the hard "rag" default

g.text: Routing and dispatch — orchestrate.decide, router.route_request, both fallbacks and the hard "rag" default
GPU — two independent vLLM endpoints, neither health-gated on this path
A · Pre-flight: should this turn be an agent turn, or use web search?
[effort permits nothing, or the message is blank]
F1 — this call sits ahead of the very first `status` frame on every text
no timeout of its own**. The
only bound is the shared 300 s httpx client timeout (config.py:264 applied
at llm.py:78). A wedged router endpoint therefore means 300 s of a
completely silent UI before anything is emitted.
— the extractor is a greedy `\{.*\}` (orchestrate.py:38) with no
think-block and no code-fence stripping, unlike router.py and agent.py; two
JSON objects in the output span from the first brace to the last and fail.
Both parse failure and transport failure land in the same bare
a dead GPU and a malformed answer are
B · Engine dispatch — first match wins (main.py:551-643)
The nine-branch chain in front of the graph, in source order:
and only then the LangGraph fallback (main.py:551-643). The router below is
on the last branch: salesforce mode, no attachment, no
B1 · Primary classification on the small model
[primary raised — connection refused, 400 window error or read timeout]
All three causes are handled identically and **nothing is logged
B2 · Retry on the MAIN model
thinking preamble is expected here — and max_tokens 50 can be consumed
, leaving parse_route nothing to match. This
retry is far more likely to fail than the primary it is covering for.
Neither call has a timeout of its own:
`rg wait_for|timeout` over engines/*.py hits only url.py:36 and
search.py:315/338. The single bound is LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 300 s
that 600 s is *on top of* the up-to-300 s already spent in step A.
There is no retry beyond this one hop, no circuit breaker, and **no
confidence score at all**: parse_route returns a route or None; no
threshold, probability or logprob exists anywhere in the file.
Consequence of the default: a total classifier outage silently sends
greetings and small talk into the vector-search engine.
F2 — the think-strip is defeated on exactly the path where it matters.
parse_route's strict branch reads the stripped text `t` (router.py:66) but
the lenient regex branch searches the
(router.py:77), so a route word mentioned inside a think block can win over
B3 · Conditional edge to exactly five nodes
in the edge map — a route outside ROUTES
would be a LangGraph KeyError. The only thing preventing it is
parse_route's membership check (router.py:71-73) plus the "rag" default,
i.e. correctness by construction rather than by guard. Every engine node
state["emit"] and state["message"] are read with bracket access
(graph.py:47,54,62,70,80-81) — a missing key surfaces as the terminal
`error` event. No timeouts, no retries in graph.py.
ChatState declares `route`, but main.py never reads it — the route the UI
displays comes from the engine's own meta payload, not from graph state.
Red-bordered box = trust boundary / risk zone.
Solid arrow = call · dashed arrow = return value.
Red note = swallowed exception, missing timeout or silent degradation.
Amber note = design constraint worth auditing.
Fn labels are the finding ids from docs/_evidence/orch-engines-core4.md.
